name: vwap_slope_momentum_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: VWAP slope (rate of change of VWAP) reflects the average price trajectory weighted by volume — it's a volume-weighted trend indicator. When VWAP slope is steep and price stays above VWAP, institutional accumulation is likely in progress. The inefficiency exists because most traders look at VWAP level (above/below) but not VWAP slope. Not fully arbitraged because VWAP slope calculation requires continuous recalculation and is non-trivial.
mechanism: VWAP is the institutional execution benchmark. When spot deviates significantly from session VWAP, algorithmic execution engines increase order flow to mean-revert their fills toward VWAP. This creates measurable gravitational pull, especially during lower-volume mid-session periods when fewer competing flows are present.

indicators.name: vwap_slope
indicators.purpose: VWAP slope in bps per bar

exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_slope_zscore drops below 0.5 (for longs)

weaknesses: VWAP slope is noisy early in the session when cumulative volume is low. The 30-min no-trade filter helps but doesn't eliminate early noise.
Late-entry problem: by the time VWAP slope z-score sustains at 1.5+ for 5 bars, a significant portion of the move is done.
VWAP slope naturally flattens as the day progresses (cumulative average effect). The signal becomes weaker in the afternoon by construction.
prior_art: VWAP slope analysis is less common in literature. Closest: institutional VWAP execution literature and TWAP benchmarking.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
